messages:
maya: FYI canary rollout for release/PR #4321 (fused-schedule) is showing decode p95 +18% on A100 tests. @owen can you triage?

perf-ci-bot: CI perf alert: job=gke-inference/canary-a100[run-824] — decode_p95: baseline=38.2ms -> canary=45.1ms (+18.1%). Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/824

owen: on it. pausing canary rollouts, marking canary hold. assigning bisect.

infra-bot: Canary rollout for release/PR-4321 paused by @owen :warning:

owen: ran a quick bisect across canary commits, narrowed to commit abc1234 (merge of sree/fuse-op-scheduler). Reproduces on local A100 with small repro.

li: uploaded profiler snapshot -> https://perf.redwood/reports/2176000123/flame.html. Key diff from baseline:
```
attn_kernel_forward: 11.8ms -> 19.6ms (+66%)
decoder_loop: 2.9ms -> 4.3ms (+48%)
kv_cache_memcpy: 0.4ms -> 0.6ms (+50%)
```

ana: interesting. looks like the kernel chooser is preferring the fused-attn kernel which is slower for short sequences. maybe heuristic regression.

owen: confirmed: kernel_selector chose 'fused_attn_v2' for seq<=64. baseline used 'attn_unfused_fast' which was better for batch sizes 1-4.

sree: that patch changed schedule heuristics to reduce kernel launch overhead for long sequences; missed perf cliff for short seqs. my bad.

maya: options: revert abc1234, or add runtime flag to prefer attn_unfused_fast for seq<=128. revert preferred for immediate rollback.

owen: opened revert PR #4330. link: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4330. will run canary after revert.

perf-ci-bot: Running canary tests for PR #4330... decode_p95: baseline=38.2ms -> revert=39.1ms (+2.4%) — within noise.

infra-bot: Canary rollout resumed and passed smoke checks.

sree: will follow up with a targeted fix for kernel_selector heuristics and add unit perf test to CI for short-seq cases.

li: adding a micro-benchmark to perf suite; also tagging an alert rule to catch seq<=128 decode_p95 regressions.

maya: thanks all. retro action: add a perf gating check on merges touching kernel selection and add perf test matrix for batch sizes 1-4.

owen: sounds good. closing thread once revert is merged and canary stable.

maya: revert merged, canary stable. closing. :white_check_mark:
